                    ### Question
                    An endocervical swab is performed and nucleic acid amplification testing via polymerase chain reaction is conducted. It is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Intravenous cefoxitin plus oral doxycycline
opb. Intramuscular ceftriaxone
opc. Intramuscular ceftriaxone plus oral azithromycin
opd. Oral azithromycin
ope. Oral doxycycline

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Chlamydia trachomatis infection requires antibiotic treatment. Since the endocervical swab was positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy would be oral azithromycin, which is effective against Chlamydia trachomatis. Dual therapy with azithromycin and doxycycline is also a consideration for possible co-infection.
